provenance.note: The closed list of partially exempt industries referenced by 1904.2(a)(1). Codes are NAICS INDUSTRY GROUPS (4 digits); an establishment's own code is usually 6 digits, so the match is on its first four. eCFR titles this a NON-MANDATORY appendix, but it is the operative list 1904.2 points at.
provenance.verification_note: Transcribed from the eCFR text of Appendix A to Subpart B. Every code and title is verbatim. NAICS VINTAGE IS UNRESOLVED: the appendix was last amended at 79 FR 56186 (Sept. 18, 2014) and 1904.2(b)(2)(iii) refers to a 1987 SIC to 2002 NAICS concordance, so an establishment holding a code from a later NAICS revision may not map cleanly onto these four-digit groups. Confirm the vintage before relying on a borderline match.

match_rule.rule: Take the first four digits of the establishment's NAICS code and look them up. A six-digit code such as 621111 falls under industry group 6211 and is therefore exempt.

defeated_by.rule: The exemption does not apply if the employer is asked IN WRITING to keep records by OSHA, the Bureau of Labor Statistics, OR A STATE AGENCY operating under the authority of OSHA or the BLS. The appendix names state agencies explicitly, where 1904.1(a)(1) mentions only OSHA and BLS.

survives_exemption.rule: All employers, INCLUDING those partially exempted by reason of company size or industry classification, must report to OSHA any employee's fatality, in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye.
